description: Clamping unit force, position and pivot inspection — PROC-63

box_1.text: Complete the following checks: 1. Inspect the clamping arm bodies for cracks or bending deformation. 2. Check each pivot pin boss for looseness by attempting to rock the arm. 3. Inspect the clamping pad faces for wear beyond the minimum thickness.

box_2.text: Cracks, deformation or severe wear on clamping arms?

box_3.text: End, Replace clamping unit: structural failure detected

box_4.text: Place a calibrated load cell between the clamping pad face and a rigid reference block positioned at the nominal part contact surface height. Close the clamp to the production pressure setting and record the peak force from the load cell amplifier display. Repeat the measurement at all clamping stations and compare each reading against the minimum and maximum clamp force in the fixturing specification.

box_5.text: Refer to the clamping force specification.

box_6.text: Clamping force within ±5% of rated value?

box_7.text: Replace return springs and check actuator seals

box_8.text: Reverify clamping force after spring replacement

box_9.text: End, Escalate: actuator servicing required, force unrecoverable

box_10.text: Using a surface roughness tester, scan the clamp pad contact face in two perpendicular directions and record the Ra value. Compare against the maximum permitted roughness in the pad specification; an excessively rough pad will mark soft part materials. Using a calibrated surface plate and a dial gauge, measure flatness of the pad at four corner points and compare against the flatness tolerance.

box_12.text: Replace clamp pad, apply correct torque to retaining screws

box_13.text: Command the clamp to the fully open position and measure the gap between the pad face and the reference surface using a digital caliper; compare against the nominal open position dimension. Close the clamp fully and probe the closed position sensor at its trigger point using a feeler gauge to measure the sensor actuation gap. Both values must fall within the tolerance ranges on the clamp setup drawing.

box_14.text: Refer to the clamping position tolerance.

box_15.text: Open and close sensor positions within ±0.3 mm of nominal?

box_16.text: Reposition sensors and reteach open/close positions in programmable controller

box_18.text: End, Escalate: mechanical stop position shifted, datum check required

box_19.text: Mount a dial test indicator against the pivot pin boss with the clamp arm loaded against its return spring. Measure the lateral displacement of the pin within the bore by applying a load perpendicular to the pin axis and recording the indicator reading. Compare the measured radial play against the maximum pin to bore clearance in the clamp specification; excessive play indicates worn pin or bore requiring replacement.

box_20.text: Pivot pin radial clearance within 0.05 mm limit?

box_21.text: Replace worn pivot pins and ream bore to H7 tolerance

box_22.text: Inspect each grease nipple on the pivot point assemblies for proper seating of the ball check valve by pressing the tip of a grease gun nozzle and confirming the nipple accepts grease. Apply two strokes of the specified grease grade to each nipple. Cycle the clamp arm through three full open and close strokes to distribute the lubricant before wiping excess from the pad face.

box_23.text: Refer to the clamping unit lubrication specification.

box_25.text: Apply grease to all pivot pin nipples, quantity per spec

box_26.text: Set the clamp controller to automatic cycle mode and command 20 consecutive open and close cycles at production speed. Monitor the cycle for consistent motion, absence of mechanical shock at end of stroke, and correct sensor signals at each position. Record the cycle time and compare against the target cycle time; an increase greater than 15% indicates hydraulic or pneumatic system degradation.

box_27.text: All 20 cycles completed without missed clamp or timeout?

box_28.text: Investigate cycle fault, check sensor and actuator timing

box_29.text: Complete the following steps: 1. Load the reference part into the fixture and close the clamp to production pressure. 2. Attempt to move the reference part by applying a lateral force by hand. 3. Confirm the part does not move and record the clamping force reading.

box_30.text: Reference part held without movement during simulated cut?

box_31.text: Log clamp force and cycle data, update service record

box_33.text: Secondary spring set replacement: remove all clamping springs and verify the spring seat surfaces are clean and undamaged before fitting. Install new springs from the correct specification batch, confirming the free length of each spring matches the specification before installation. Cycle the clamp five times after replacement to allow the springs to seat before returning to the clamping force measurement step.
